 SSC GD 2026: Physical Date, Vacancy Increase, Score Card Date & Latest Update
 SSC GD selection process has several stages. Candidates must qualify in the written exam before moving to the Physical Standard Test (PST) and Physical Efficiency Test (PET). Around 25,000 posts are available in the current cycle.  No chance of a major increase in the vacancies. In previous years, candidates usually got about 30 to 75 days to prepare for the physical test after the written result.

 The Staff Selection Commission (SSC) conducts the General Duty (GD) examination for recruitment in various Central Armed Police Forces. The current recruitment cycle has around 25,000 vacancies.
 A large number of candidates appear for the SSC GD examination every year. After the written examination, selected candidates are called for the Physical Standard Test and Physical Efficiency Test. Therefore, physical preparation is important for candidates who qualify for the next stage.
 SSC GD Vacancy: Will the Number of Posts Increase?
 The current SSC GD recruitment has around 25,000 vacancies. There is very little possibility of a major increase in the number of posts in the present cycle.
 Some changes were made in the list of candidates selected for the physical stage because of category-related issues. Candidates from reserved categories such as SC, ST and OBC were found in the General category in some cases. SSC later released a revised list of shortlisted candidates.
 However, the revised list did not mean that the total number of vacancies was increased. The available posts and required selection standards remained in place.
 The next recruitment cycle may have a different number of vacancies. The vacancy number for a future cycle will depend on the official SSC notification.

 The past dates show that the gap can be different in every recruitment cycle. In many cases, candidates get about one to two months for physical preparation.
 Candidates should not wait for the physical date before starting training. Running practice, stamina building and other exercises should be started early.
 SSC GD Physical Test: PST and PET
 Candidates who qualify for the written examination are called for the Physical Standard Test and Physical Efficiency Test mentioned in the SSC GD Selection Process .  
 The PST checks physical measurements such as height and chest. The PET mainly checks running and physical endurance.

 SSC GD Medical Examination
 Candidates who clear the physical stages must also meet the required medical standards.
 The medical examination may check eyesight, general fitness and other health-related requirements. Candidates can get their height, chest measurement and eyesight checked in advance at a suitable medical centre.
 An early check can help identify problems that may need attention before the official medical examination.

 SSC GD Score Card: When Will It Come?
 The SSC GD score card is released by SSC as part of the result process. The exact date depends on the official result schedule.
 Candidates should check the SSC website and official notices for the score card release date. The score card can provide details such as marks and other result-related information.

 SSC GD 2026 FAQs
 Will SSC GD vacancies increase?
 There is less chance of a major increase in the current vacancies. The present recruitment has around 25,000 posts, but the final vacancy figure should be checked in the latest official SSC notice. How much time is available between the written result and physical test?
 It is available around 30 to 75 days. What is the required height for SSC GD?
 The general height requirement is 170 cm for male candidates and 157 cm for female candidates. Some categories may have different standards as per SSC rules. What is the SSC GD running requirement?
 Male candidates generally have to complete a 5 km run within 24 minutes. Female candidates generally have to complete a 1.6 km run within 8.5 minutes. Is chest measurement required for female candidates?
 The chest measurement requirement applies to male candidates. The general requirement is a minimum chest measurement of 80 cm with 5 cm expansion. Have questions about your prep?
